detail:
The Arthritis Foundation describes its Rheumatoid Arthritis Research Program as focused on the biological underpinnings of RA, including immune system dysfunction, risk factors for disease progression, and related conditions. Its 2025 awards fund projects at academic centers studying how immune responses and early joint changes differ in people with RA.

Directions the Foundation highlights include how B cells behave as preclinical RA becomes clinical disease, the root causes of treatment resistance in refractory RA, which it describes as persistent disease that does not respond as expected, and the link between neurotrophins, proteins involved in nerve growth, and RA pain. The Foundation frames this work as aiming to predict development and progression, explain non-response to treatment, and eventually support prevention and better therapies.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about rheumatoid arthritis research directions.

summary: The Arthritis Foundation describes its 2025 rheumatoid arthritis research awards, funding projects on immune mechanisms, the shift from preclinical to clinical disease, and treatment-resistant RA.
takeaways: funded projects study immune mechanisms behind ra
researchers are studying how preclinical ra becomes clinical disease
treatment-resistant, or refractory, ra is a research priority
pain mechanisms in ra are an active area of study
title: Where rheumatoid arthritis research is heading
